title: Cold rebuild: motions in real Vim
summary: Strip trailing comments with motions inside :normal in real Vim, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Lines, characters and jumps* you used motions inside `:normal` in real Vim to strip
trailing comments. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks
are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson, then try
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The line is `name = "value"` with the cursor on `n`. Which keys put the cursor on the `e` that ends `value`?
steps.explain: `$` reaches the closing quote and `h` steps back one. Three `e`s stop at `name`, `=`, then the opening quote; two `f"` land on the closing quote.

steps.title: Strip trailing comments, cold
prompt: In `~/servers.conf`, remove every trailing comment and the spaces before it, with Vim (`vim -es`). Lines that are only a comment stay.
From memory: no hints this time.
